_readme: Illustrative development and demo data. The values are plausible for the products named but are not measurements, and the taxonomy sources are placeholders. The laptop record is labelled after its photographs (HP logo, ProBook palm rest, mainboard marked ZPM30 LA-B171P); its display size, dimensions, the 1.6 kg configuration weight and the brushed aluminium keyboard deck follow HP QuickSpecs c04333719 (HP ProBook 430 G2 Notebook PC, https://h20195.www2.hp.com/v2/GetDocument.aspx?docname=c04333719), and every other value is illustrative.

product_data.name: HP ProBook 430 G2
product_data.description: Illustrative seed record, not a measured teardown. HP business laptop, as shown in the photographs.

circularity_properties.recyclability: Illustrative note. A brushed aluminium keyboard deck is typically recoverable once the boards are out; a bonded glass-and-polymer display stack typically is not separated.
circularity_properties.disassemblability: Illustrative note. Laptops of this build typically open through a service door on the underside.
circularity_properties.remanufacturability: Illustrative note. Display assembly, keyboard and SSD are candidates for reuse as whole parts; the mainboard would need testing first.

components.name: Display assembly
components.description: Lid, bezel, hinges and LCD panel as one removable unit.

circularity_properties.recyclability: Illustrative note. Panel glass bonded to a polymer frame typically is not separated, so the panel goes to WEEE processing whole.
circularity_properties.disassemblability: Illustrative note. The bezel typically comes off before the panel does; hinges typically unscrew.
circularity_properties.remanufacturability: Illustrative note. Reusable as a whole assembly if the hinge mounts are undamaged.

components.name: Lid and hinges
components.description: Painted lid with both hinges attached.

components.description: Sheet-metal service door from the underside, inner face up.

components.name: Keyboard

circularity_properties.recyclability: Illustrative note. A populated board typically goes to WEEE processing whole, after its coin-cell battery is taken out.
circularity_properties.disassemblability: Illustrative note. The board typically unscrews from the top cover once its ribbon connectors unlatch.
